question.text: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is dropped from the height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The height, at which the magnitude of velocity becomes equal to the magnitude of acceleration due to gravity, is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. [Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ]

solution.text:
Consider downward direction to be positive.

Applying first equation of motion, v=u+at

⇒v=0+gt ⇒g=gt ⇒t=1 s 

Distance covered in 1 s, s=ut+12at2=0+12g×12=102=5 m

Hence, height of the point from the surface =10-5 m=5 m
